metadata.note: The Virginia and Southwestern Railway (George L. Carter's road, formed 1899 from the South Atlantic and Ohio and the Bristol, Elizabethton and North Carolina) and its Southern Railway successor, the Appalachia Division (from July 1916). Lines: Bristol - Big Stone Gap - Appalachia (the 'Natural Tunnel Route'), Appalachia - St. Charles, Bristol - Elizabethton - Mountain City (the Tennessee Division), the Stony Creek Branch, the Holston River Line (Moccasin Gap - Coran - Bulls Gap) and Bulls Gap - Rogersville. Features split at each operator change under Rule 4: SA&O / BE&NC to V&SW in 1899, V&SW to Southern in July 1916. The Southern's 1906 purchase of control is NOT a split - the V&SW ran its own trains until July 1916. Each drawn span is the research report's drawable: span. Handover years (1899, 1916) appear on both the outgoing and incoming feature, as drawn by the report; segment years are inclusive.
sources: Big Stone Gap Post on Chronicling America (sn88061179): timetables of 1893, 1900, 1905, 1908, 1909, 1917
Bristol / Johnson City Comet on Chronicling America (sn89058128, sn98069795)
John Fowler, Virginia and Tennessee Railroads Passenger Stations (branchline.uk): https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/virginiarrs.pdf, https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/tennesseerrs.pdf
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952: https://archive.org/download/the-official-guide-of-the-railways-images/The%20Official%20Guide%20of%20the%20Railways_djvu.txt
not_yet_sourced: Main line passenger end: 1939 (Virginia DCR; HMdb Duffield marker as summarised) vs 1947 (Wikipedia Mendota Trail, uncited) vs 'late 1940s' (HMdb summary). Drawn to 1939.
[OPEN] southern-appalachia-st-charles: confirmed only to 1934; real end unknown (probably 1939 with the main line, unproven).
[OPEN] southern-bristol-mountain-city: confirmed only to 1934; the Aug 1940 flood is a hard ceiling for Elizabethton - Mountain City; Bristol - Elizabethton passenger end unknown.
[OPEN] vsw-stony-creek-branch: confirmed only to 1909 (end of the Chronicling America run of the schedule); no Southern-era evidence.
[OPEN START] vsw-holston-river-line: opening bracket 1910-1914, drawn from the first confirmed year 1914; whether the Holston River Railway ran trains in its own name 1910-1916 is unknown.
[OPEN] southern-holston-river-line: confirmed only to 1917; freight only by Sept 1951.

[OPEN] southern-bulls-gap-rogersville: confirmed at 1917 and 1952 only; post-1952 end unknown; pre-1916 ETV&G/Southern years not drawn; whether the V&SW operated it 1910-1916 (Fowler's 'ex VSW') is unresolved.
[ANCHOR] bena-bristol-elizabethton: only Jan 1899 proven; BE&NC passenger start (1892? 1898?) unknown.
SA&O pre-1890 stub Bristol - Gate City (open into Scott County by Jan 1888): passenger service not established, not drawn.
The Southern-era Stony Creek Branch (report block [10]) has no passenger evidence and is omitted.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn. Bristol - Appalachia - St. Charles was freight only by Sept 1951 and is trimmed at 1939 / 1934 [OPEN]; the Holston River Line at 1917 [OPEN]; Bristol - Elizabethton after 1934 is not drawn. Coal spurs (Keokee branch, Black Mountain spurs) and Big Stone Gap's separate Dummy Line are not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: None: all lines were steam from opening.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py on 2026-10-27; 66.4 mi Bristol - Big Stone Gap against 66.5 mi documented (Fowler, Big Stone Gap MP 66.5), NO straight-line legs. Bristol - Mendota is the lifted grade, now the Mendota Trail (OSM highway=cycleway + railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=Southern, note:old_railway_operator=Virginia and Southwestern); Mendota - Big Stone Gap is live Norfolk Southern track (NS Appalachia District, same tags). Traced mileposts: Mendota 14.5, Hiltons 23.4, Moccasin Gap 29.2, Gate City 31.1, Speers Ferry 39.6, Natural Tunnel 45.2, Duffield 50.1. The trace stays off the Clinchfield where the two cross near Speers Ferry (0 mi on Clinchfield-tagged ways). The last few hundred metres into Bristol station use untagged/Southern-tagged station trackage. CAVEAT (Rule 2): this draws the surviving modern alignment for the 1890s; any later realignment of the SA&O/V&SW line is not identified or backed out.

segments.note: First passenger train through to Big Stone Gap in May 1890 (Clio; Wikipedia Mendota Trail; Virginia DCR Natural Tunnel brochure: 'both the first passenger train and coal train travelled through the tunnel in 1890'); the Bristol Courier/Comet of 28 Aug 1890 already speaks of 'the freight and passenger business of the South Atlantic and Ohio'. The SA&O's own timetable in the Big Stone Gap Post, 2 Feb 1893, runs trains 1-4 Big Stone Gap - Bristol. Ends 1899, when the Virginia and Southwestern bought the property. An earlier stub reached Scott County / Gate City c.1887-88, but passenger service on it is not confirmed and is not drawn. Source conflict recorded: Wikipedia's Natural Tunnel State Park article puts the first train through the tunnel in 1894, which the 1890 newspaper and 1893 timetable contradict. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the number of trains in the cited timetable, not a measured headway; avg_speed_kmh is likewise an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: dates from the 1893 SA&O timetable (Big Stone Gap Post 2 Feb 1893), Comet 28 Aug 1890, Clio, Virginia DCR, as read in research/branches/virginia_and_southwestern_railway.txt block [1].

segments.note: V&SW ('The Natural Tunnel Route') from the 1899 purchase of the SA&O; first V&SW timetable seen is dated 9 Sept 1900 (Big Stone Gap Post 27 Sept 1900). Schedules of Dec 1908 and Sept 1909 run Bristol - Appalachia (Union Station, with the L&N), with trains 1 and 2 carrying a Pullman drawing-room buffet sleeper Bristol - Louisville 'without change' over the L&N. The Southern bought control in 1906, but the V&SW kept running its own trains, timetables and staff until July 1916, when it was abolished and made the Southern's Appalachia Division (Johnson City Comet, 20 July 1916) - so 1916 also begins the Southern feature. In receivership 1901. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the number of trains in the cited timetable, not a measured headway; avg_speed_kmh is likewise an unsourced estimate.

segments.note: Southern Railway Appalachia Division from July 1916. Passenger evidence: the Feb 1917 'Southern Railway System, Condensed Time Card' (Nos. 1-4 Bristol - Appalachia - St. Charles, the Louisville Pullman sleeper still running); a 1934 Bristol schedule (SOU Local #1 / #4 to and from Appalachia and St. Charles). The train was later the 'Lonesome Pine Special'. END YEAR IS A SOURCE CONFLICT: 1939 per two Virginia DCR Natural Tunnel park documents ('In 1939, the passenger service ended') and an HMdb Duffield marker as summarised; 1947 per Wikipedia's Mendota Trail article (uncited); 'late 1940s' per another HMdb marker (summary only). Drawn to 1939, the earlier and better-sourced year. Freight only by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 43 station daggers). Coal traffic continued; Norfolk Southern still runs Mendota - Appalachia. Headway is an estimate (two trains each way in 1917, one in 1934); avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the Feb 1917 Southern time card, the 1934 Bristol schedule, the Virginia DCR documents and the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 43, as read in the research report block [3].

OSM holds only one piece of this grade: way 169328881 (railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=Southern, note:old_railway_operator=Virginia and Southwestern), 1.5 mi traced near Keenburg. OpenHistoricalMap has nothing in the corridor. Approximated legs, all STRAIGHT LINES: Bristol Union Station - Bluff City 9.3 mi (documented 11.9); Bluff City - Keenburg (north end of the OSM way) 4.4 mi; Keenburg (south end of the OSM way) - Elizabethton town centre 3.4 mi. The straight legs are deliberately NOT snapped onto the Southern's Bristol - Knoxville main line (knoxville_early_railroads.geojson), which passes Bluff City on separate track; between Bristol and Bluff City the chord runs close to it. The Bristol end is drawn at Bristol Union Station; the Tennessee Division's own Bristol (Scranton St.) station is not located. The ~3.8 mi shortfall is the straight legs cutting the curves.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year. The Comet of 12 Jan 1899, quoting the Bristol Courier: 'three engines are kept busy handling freight coke and passengers' (coke for the Johnson City and Embreeville furnaces). Service certainly ran wider than this one year in some form, but no other year of BE&NC passenger service is confirmed: in Aug 1892 the road was not yet 'in running order', and in Feb 1896 its two locomotives were sold by the trustee. southern-railroads.org's 'Operated: 1892 to 1940' cites nothing. George Carter bought the road in 1899 and merged it into the V&SW, so 1899 overlaps the V&SW feature on these rails. Do not widen this anchor without evidence. headway_min is a placeholder estimate; no BE&NC timetable was found.
sources: Segment-level: the Comet of 12 Jan 1899 (passengers), 25 Aug 1892 and 13 Feb 1896, as read in the research report block [6].

properties.geometry_quality: APPROXIMATED, valley-following. 31.2 mi drawn Elizabethton - Maymead against 30.8 mi documented (Fowler table 54, MP 22.4 - 53.2). The line was destroyed by the Aug 1940 flood and its grade between the Watauga gorge and Butler is now under Watauga Lake (TVA, 1948); OSM has no rail, abandoned or razed ways for it and OpenHistoricalMap has nothing. Drawn instead along OSM WATERWAY CENTRELINES - the Watauga River from Elizabethton up through the gorge (Siam, Wilbur, Watauga Dam) and the river's drowned channel through Watauga Lake to the Roan Creek mouth at the old Butler townsite, then up Roan Creek to Maymead - Douglas-Peucker simplified at 120 m to take out meanders. This is NOT rail geometry: it says the line ran up these valleys (as the timetable stations Stony Creek Jct, Butler and Maymead show) but not on which bank or through which cuts and tunnels. Legs: Elizabethton town centre - Watauga River 0.5 mi straight, then river centreline to the Stony Creek confluence (Stony Creek Jct / Rexford) 3.9 mi total vs 3.3 documented (Fowler MP 22.4 - 25.7); Stony Creek Jct - Butler - Maymead 27.3 mi along the Watauga / lake channel / Roan Creek, ending with a short straight leg from the creek to the Maymead hamlet node. Old Butler is placed where the drowned channel passes nearest the relocated Butler (2.3 km off), an estimate.

segments.note: Tennessee Division, second stage: confirmed open by 9 Sept 1900, when the V&SW timetable runs Maymead - Butler - Stony Creek Jct - Elizabethton - Bristol (trains 3, 4, 11, 12). On 7 March 1901 the line still ended at Maymead. A July 1916 flood washed out the V&SW bridge at Butler. Ends July 1916 with the absorption into the Southern. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the number of trains in the cited timetable, not a measured headway; avg_speed_kmh is likewise an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the V&SW timetable of Sept 1900 and the Comet of 7 Mar 1901, as read in the research report block [7].

properties.geometry_quality: APPROXIMATED, valley-following. 10.7 mi drawn Rexford (Stony Creek Jct) - Buladeen against 11.0 mi documented (Fowler table 55, MP 25.7 - 36.7). OSM has no rail, abandoned or razed ways for the branch and OpenHistoricalMap has nothing; drawn along the OSM centreline of Stony Creek from its Watauga River confluence (taken as Stony Creek Jct, by Hunter) past Winner and Sadie, Douglas-Peucker simplified at 120 m, with a short straight leg from the creek to the Buladeen hamlet node. NOT rail geometry: it shows the valley the branch ran up, not the grade itself.

segments.note: Rexford (Stony Creek Junction) - Buladeen, a lumber and mining branch. 1905 confirmed: the V&SW notice of 18 May 1905 announces 'double daily first class passenger, express and mail service on Stony Creek Branch which has heretofore been practically without such accommodations', Buladeen being the terminus of 'the new Stony Creek extension'. Dec 1908 / Sept 1909: 'STONY CREEK BRANCH - Mixed, daily, except Sunday', Bristol (Scranton St.) - Buladeen. [OPEN] Confirmed to 1909, when the Big Stone Gap Post's run of the schedule on Chronicling America stops (last 8 Dec 1909). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. No Southern-era passenger evidence was found, so nothing is drawn for the branch after 1916. headway_min is an estimate (one mixed train each way, 1908-09; 'double daily' in 1905); avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the V&SW notice of 18 May 1905 and the schedules of Dec 1908 and Sept 1909 in the Big Stone Gap Post, as read in the research report block [9].

Live NS track ('NS Appalachia District'), tagged old_railway_operator=Southern + note:old_railway_operator=Virginia and Southwestern. Coran is located as the point where this line meets the Bulls Gap - Rogersville line (36.3609, -83.0122). Modern alignment drawn for 1914 on.

segments.note: Moccasin Gap - Coran (Persia Junction), built as the Holston River Railway and bought by the V&SW in 1908, 'nearly graded'. On 14 Jan 1910 track was laid on both ends but 'none of the line already constructed is yet being operated'. [OPEN START] The first confirmed passenger year is 1914 (Fowler cites a 1914 V&SW company timetable for McCloud); the opening bracket is 1910-1914, and 1914 is the earliest CONFIRMED year, not a known opening - do not move it earlier without evidence. Whether the Holston River Railway ran trains in its own name before 1916 is not established. Ends July 1916 (to the Southern). headway_min is an estimate; avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler's tennesseerrs table 57 (McCloud 1914 V&SW timetable) and the 1908-1911 newspaper notices on construction, as read in the research report block [11].

Traced mileposts from Moccasin Gap: Church Hill 14.0, Surgoinsville 22.9, McCloud 34.3, Persia 38.5. Shares Coran - Bulls Gap with the Rogersville feature. Modern alignment.

segments.note: Moccasin Gap - Coran - Bulls Gap under the Southern's Appalachia Division from July 1916. The Feb 1917 time card: No. 4 from St. Charles 'connects at Gate City for Holston River Line, Bulls Gap and Rogersville'; No. 8 'leaves Gate City 1:50 p.m. for Holston River points. Arrives Bulls Gap ..., Rogersville ...'. [OPEN] Confirmed to 1917. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped, anywhere from 1917 to 1951. Do not extend without evidence (and do NOT write 1951: the line was freight only by Sept 1951 per the Feb 1952 Official Guide's Table 42 daggers, which is a ceiling, not an end date). headway_min is an estimate; avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the Feb 1917 Southern time card and the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 42, as read in the research report block [12].

segments.note: Rogersville Branch (ex-Rogersville & Jefferson / ETV&G), run by the Southern's Appalachia Division. Drawn here only from July 1916, the Appalachia Division era; its earlier ETV&G/Southern years belong with that railroad's research and are NOT drawn yet. Anchors: the Feb 1917 time card runs Holston River trains through to Bulls Gap and Rogersville; the Feb 1952 Official Guide, Southern Table 27 'BULLS GAP AND ROGERSVILLE (Appalachia Division)', dated 20 Jan 1952, has a Mixed train No. 9 leaving Bulls Gap 9.30 A.M. (index: Persia and Coran, no dagger). The years between are unproven but nothing suggests a gap. [OPEN] 1952 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when the mixed train stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The reading of Table 27 is from a scrambled OCR page and should be rechecked against a page image. headway_min is an estimate (one mixed train); avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the Feb 1917 Southern time card and the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 27 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 105673-105700), as read in the research report block [13].
